title: Scenario suite manifest
description: Shared description of the deployment under test: the external systems scenarios read/write and the midPoint tasks they trigger. Binds the logical names scenarios use to concrete systems (suite data, not engine config).

timeoutMs.description: Max ms to wait for this task's fresh run to finish — overrides POLL_TIMEOUT_MS for a slow/cold recon.

fileName.description: File name under the host CSV dir.

idColumn.description: Identifier column for delta ops and account lookup.

midpointSystem.description: A midPoint instance scenarios drive (REST + GUI) and a restore participant (cache-clear after rollback). Connection/credentials via env-var NAMES; version is PER INSTANCE (a deployment's midPoints may differ) and selects BOTH the cache-clear payload and the GUI page-object module.

baseUrlEnv.description: Env var name holding the base URL (up to /midpoint).

usernameEnv.description: Env var name holding the admin username (may differ per environment).

passwordEnv.description: Env var name holding the admin password.

version.description: midPoint major version (e.g. "4.10", "4.4") — selects the version-correct cache-clear payload AND the GUI reference page objects.

guiBaseUrlEnv.description: Env var name holding the GUI base URL when it differs from baseUrlEnv (e.g. an SSO front-end on another origin). Omit when REST and GUI share the origin.

overrides.description: Project page-object override module path (relative to the suite dir) for this instance's customised screens.

auth.description: GUI login provider for THIS instance. Omitted/midpoint = the version's native form; keycloak = OIDC/Keycloak SSO login.

keycloakSystem.description: A Keycloak instance (restore participant; realm/user/keys cache-clear after rollback). Admin connection via env-var NAMES — EITHER a service-account client_credentials grant (secretEnv) OR a password grant (admin-cli + master admin: usernameEnv/passwordEnv, authRealmEnv=master). Can ALSO be an assert-only target (read a realm user) — declare attributes/mask to opt in.

urlEnv.description: Env var name holding the Keycloak base URL (incl. any servlet path).

realmEnv.description: Env var name holding the realm the admin operations TARGET (whose caches are cleared / users are read).

clientIdEnv.description: Env var name holding the admin client id (service-account client, or admin-cli for password grant).

secretEnv.description: Env var name holding the client secret (client_credentials grant). Omit for password grant.

usernameEnv.description: Env var name holding the admin username (password grant, INSTEAD of secretEnv).

passwordEnv.description: Env var name holding the admin password (password grant).

authRealmEnv.description: Env var name holding the realm to AUTHENTICATE against (default: the target realm; master for admin-cli).

attributes.description: Fields to project when reading this Keycloak as an assert target (allowlist). Each name matches a top-level user field (email/enabled/firstName/…) OR a custom realm-user attribute. Omit to capture all non-volatile fields.

mask.description: Field/attribute names whose volatile value is masked to a stable token (assert presence, not value). Case-sensitive.

scimSystem.description: A SCIM 2.0 Service Provider, asserted read-only (midPoint provisions outbound; the end-state lives here). Fetches a resource by a SCIM filter (<filterAttr> eq "<id>"). Auth via EITHER a bearer token (tokenEnv) OR HTTP Basic (username + passwordEnv).

url.description: Service Provider base URL incl. the version segment, e.g. https://host/scim/v2. No credential in it.

tokenEnv.description: Bearer-token auth: env var name holding the token. Use this XOR Basic (username + passwordEnv).

username.description: HTTP Basic auth: the user name (not secret).

passwordEnv.description: HTTP Basic auth: env var name holding the password (the secret).

filterAttr.description: SCIM attribute the account identifier filters on (default userName).

attributes.description: Attribute PATHS to project when asserting (allowlist). A path navigates the resource by slash (name/givenName, active); the output key IS the path. Omit to assert the whole resource minus volatile fields (id/meta/schemas).

mask.description: Attribute paths whose volatile value is masked to a stable token (assert presence, not value). Case-sensitive.

resourceSystem.description: Connector-mediated midPoint resource: read/drive a target object THROUGH midPoint's connector (REST -> model -> connector), so a system idweave has no native client for (incl. proprietary connectors) can still be asserted and ARRANGEd. Generic fallback (oracle mediated by midPoint); standardized protocols keep their direct readers. Identified at the connector level by objectClass; kind/intent/tag are optional refined-schema refinements. Addressed by a focus `owner` or a standalone `identifier`. Driven through the suite's midPoint; with several midPoints, `midpoint:` names the owning instance.

name.description: midPoint resource NAME (resolved to its OID). Use this XOR oid.

objectClass.description: Native object class — the connector-level discriminator, e.g. ri:inetOrgPerson, ri:groupOfNames.

attributes.description: Shadow attributes to project when asserting (allowlist, matched by local name). Omit to capture all non-operational attributes.

mask.description: Attribute names whose volatile value is masked to a stable token (assert presence, not value).

identifierAttr.description: How an `identifier` is matched: `__uid__` (the connector PRIMARY identifier, e.g. entryUUID / a CSV key column), `__name__` (the SECONDARY identifier, e.g. an LDAP DN; absent on some connectors), or a regular attribute name (default `name`).

intent.description: Refined-schema intent (optional) — disambiguates two object types sharing one objectClass.

midpoint.description: Named midPoint instance (a suite.systems key) the resource is driven through — its version selects the connector-script dialect. Omit when the suite has a single midPoint; REQUIRED when several are declared.

url.description: URL with scheme — ldap:// (plain) or ldaps:// (TLS).

dn.description: Bind principal (DN or UPN) — not a secret.

passwordEnv.description: Name of the env var holding the bind password (the only secret).

containerDn.description: DN whose direct children are the accounts (washed/repopulated like a CSV file).

rdnAttr.description: RDN attribute, e.g. cn (AD) / uid (OpenLDAP). DN = <rdnAttr>=<row[rdnAttr]>,<containerDn>.

objectClasses.description: objectClass values for created entries; the first is also the reset filter class.

baseAttrs.description: Fixed attributes on every entry, e.g. { "userAccountControl": "544" }.

from.description: Row attribute holding the cleartext password.

to.description: Attribute receiving the encoded password (default unicodePwd).

password.description: Map a cleartext row attribute to a password attribute (AD unicodePwd: UTF-16LE, quoted).

attributes.description: Attributes to project when reading this system as a target (the assertion allowlist, like CSV columns). Omit to capture all non-operational attributes.

mask.description: Attribute names whose volatile value is masked to a stable token (assert presence, not value), e.g. x-externalRef. Case-insensitive.

consistentWith.description: Cross-system consistency (ldap attribute or db column): assert a (multi-)value equals a transform of a midPoint focus property — stronger than a static golden, since the value is volatile. The engine derives the expected from the focus at run time and compares as an order-independent, de-duplicated SET; on a match the value collapses to a token <consistent:<from>>, on a mismatch it diffs. Keyed by the attribute/column name.

from.description: Focus property path to derive the expected value(s) from (the account identifier is the user name), e.g. extension/externalRef. Multi-value supported.

listSeparator.description: Use ONLY when the TARGET system can't store multiple values natively and packs them into a SINGLE field joined by this separator (e.g. a custom attribute holding 'a,b') — the string is split by this into a set before comparison. A genuinely multi-valued attribute (an LDAP multi-value attribute is already an array) does NOT need this. Either way the comparison is an order-independent, de-duplicated set.

delimited.description: Transform method (externally tagged by this key; a future `regex` slots in beside it): split each `from` value by `delimiter` into positional fields, then build the expected value with `format` (referencing fields by name when `names` is set, else by 0-based index; literals pass through).

delimiter.description: Splits each source value into positional fields.

names.description: Optional names for the leading field positions, so `format` can use {name} (self-documenting) instead of {0}.

url.description: Connection URL; scheme selects the dialect (postgres:// default -> pg). No password in it.

passwordEnv.description: Name of the env var holding the connection password (the only secret).

query.description: Parameterized SELECT; :id binds the lookup value. Returns the asserted row(s).

update.description: Optional parameterized UPDATE for the db-mutate step (rewind external mock state). Binds :id (via linkFrom, like query) and :value (the new value the step supplies). Use cast(:value as t) not :value::t so the :name parser isn't confused by ::. Omit on read-only systems.

columns.description: Columns to project when asserting (allowlist, like LDAP attributes). Omit to assert all returned columns.

linkFrom.description: Focus linkage for rows keyed by a value midPoint holds (not a stable id). The engine runs the query once per linking value (:id = each) and asserts the union as a sorted set. Source the value(s) from EITHER `path` (read live from the focus named by the account identifier) OR `capture` (a value a capture-focus step recorded earlier) — exactly one. Omit linkFrom entirely for a plain :id=identifier lookup.

path.description: Slash path into the focus (named by the account identifier) to read the linking value(s) LIVE, e.g. extension/externalRef.

capture.description: Name of a capture-focus slot holding the linking value(s) recorded earlier — to assert a row whose value the run since destroyed (e.g. a value removed by a scheduled task).

type.description: Focus type to read for `path` (default user).

systems.description: Systems of the deployment under test, keyed by the logical name scenarios reference. Each is exactly one of csv | ldap | db | scim | resource (external read/write or assert target; resource is connector-mediated via midPoint) or midpoint | keycloak (an instance — restore participant; keycloak may also be an assert target).

triggers.description: midPoint registered tasks the `trigger` step runs, keyed by system name (midPoint-specific).

recon.description: Reconciliation task: an OID string, or { task, timeoutMs }.

import.description: Import task: an OID string, or { task, timeoutMs }.

tasks.description: Global registered midPoint tasks the `run-task` step runs, keyed by a logical name. Deployment-wide operational/scanner tasks (validity scan, cleanup), not tied to one system. Each value is a task OID.

defaultSystem.description: System a mutate/trigger step uses when it omits `system:` and there is more than one.

gui.description: Cross-cutting GUI settings (named logins, per-principal passwords). The page-object version/overrides/auth are per driven system (systems.*.midpoint), not here.

logins.description: Named logins for a suite that drives more than one login target (a midPoint dashboard, a Keycloak Account/Admin console). A login-ui step selects one by name with `to:`. Each is one (system, target route).

system.description: System this login targets — its kind/auth implies the provider + page objects. Omit for the sole/default driveable system.

target.description: Authenticated route to reach to trigger login (absolute, or a path joined to the GUI base). Default /self/dashboard.

principals.description: Per-principal GUI login passwords (only the env-var name is suite data). A login not listed falls back to GUI_PASSWORD. Lets one suite drive the GUI as users with different passwords.

passwordEnv.description: Name of the env var holding this principal's GUI password (the secret).

normalize.description: Project-declared normalization for this deployment's data.

mask.description: Focus-projection paths (a/b/c) whose volatile value is masked to a stable token.

snapshot.description: Whole-env snapshot-restore topology for the fast near-non-stop reset (any backend). Optional; env vars (SNAPSHOT_RESTORE_STOP / SNAPSHOT_RESTORE_ROLLBACK) override it, and the snapshot CLI works without it (falls back to stopping/resetting everything).

restore.description: Stop only the data-owning service(s) and pause the rest, so the heavy app is frozen (not rebooted) and recovers via its DB connection pool. The CLI auto-falls back to a full restart if a paused service restarted since the baseline.

stop.description: Compose service(s) to fully STOP around the reset (the rest are paused, not restarted).

rollback.description: Compose volume KEY(s) to reset (btrfs → subvolume under SNAPSHOT_BTRFS_DIR; tar → <project>_<key> volume). Defaults to the `stop` names.
